explanation: A way of counting part-time students or staff as fractions of a full-time one, so that schools with many part-timers can be compared with schools that have few. For staff, IPEDS adds one-third of the part-time staff to the full-time staff. For students, IPEDS has two calculations: one from fall headcounts and one from the 12-month instructional activity (credit or clock hours).
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Full-time equivalent (FTE) of staff; Full-time equivalent (FTE) of students

explanation: The group of students a rate is calculated on, after IPEDS's allowed exclusions are taken out: students who died, became permanently disabled, left for military service, a foreign aid service, or an official church mission. Graduation and retention rates divide by the adjusted cohort, not by everyone who started.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Adjusted cohort; Cohort. The list of exclusions: IPEDS Graduation Rates instructions

explanation: Retention, as IPEDS reports it, is the share of first-time students from the previous fall who are enrolled again at the same school in the current fall. At four-year schools it counts first-time bachelor's degree-seeking students; at other schools it counts first-time degree or certificate-seeking students, and students who completed their program by the current fall also count as retained. Rates are reported separately for full-time and part-time students. Persistence usually means staying enrolled anywhere, including at another school; IPEDS does not publish a persistence rate. Outcome Measures come closest, by reporting students who later enrolled at another institution.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Retention rate; Outcome Measures (OM). Persistence is not in the glossary: general explanation

words: sticker price; published tuition; total price; net price
explanation: The published (sticker) price is the cost of attendance a school lists for a full-time, first-time student: tuition and fees, food and housing, books and supplies, and other expenses. Net price is that cost of attendance minus the average grant and scholarship aid (federal, state or local, and institutional) received by first-time, full-time students awarded such aid. Loans are not subtracted. For public schools the in-state or in-district price is used. Net price is usually far lower than the published price, and IPEDS also reports it by family income.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Net price; Cost of attendance (COA)
app_convention: When you ask for net price, this app shows the average for students awarded grant or scholarship aid, unless you ask for another group.

concept: Why net price is a year behind
explanation: Net price depends on the grant and scholarship aid students were actually awarded, which is only complete after the academic year ends. So each IPEDS release reports net price for the academic year before it: the 2024-25 release reports net price for 2023-24, with the two years before that alongside.
source: IPEDS variable titles for average net price (NPIST2, NPGRN2) in each release

words: graduation rate; transfer students; 150%; normal time
explanation: The IPEDS graduation rate follows only students who started at the school as first-time, full-time students, and counts those who finished there within 150% of normal time (six years for a bachelor's degree). Students who transfer in are not in the cohort, and students who transfer out and finish elsewhere do not count as graduates. For schools whose mission includes preparing students to transfer, IPEDS also reports a transfer-out rate. Outcome Measures add part-time and transfer-in students and report awards at four, six and eight years.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Graduation rate; Normal time to completion; Transfer-out student; Transfer-out rate; Outcome Measures (OM)

explanation: Each IPEDS release is first published as provisional data, after NCES's checks. A year later it is published again as final data, which includes the corrections schools made in the meantime. The figures can change a little between the two. In this app, 2024-25 is provisional and the other nine releases are final.
source: IPEDS overview 2019 (pages 10-11, data quality and release)
app_convention: Answers from the 2024-25 release carry a note that its figures are provisional.

explanation: A school that has an agreement with the U.S. Department of Education to take part in federal student aid programs (Pell Grants and federal loans). Taking part in IPEDS is required for these schools and voluntary for others, so IPEDS is most complete for Title IV schools.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Title IV institution; IPEDS overview 2019 (page 1)
app_convention: When no group is named, this app counts the Title IV participating schools in the 50 states and DC.

explanation: The group of schools a school's own IPEDS Data Feedback Report compares it with. The school can choose it, or NCES builds it from similar schools. In this app, "its peers" means that group, as of the latest year.
source: IPEDS Data Feedback Report; the comparison groups schools submit to IPEDS (CUSTOMCGIDS)

concept: The national universe in this app
words: national universe; all U.S. schools; nationally
explanation: When no group is named, this app counts schools in the 50 states and DC that take part in Title IV federal aid, leaving out administrative offices (system offices that enroll no students). IPEDS itself also holds schools in U.S. territories and some that do not take part in Title IV.
source: IPEDS overview 2019 (page 8: the IPEDS universe); this app's own rules

words: parent; child; reports with; branch campus
explanation: Some schools report part of their IPEDS data together with another campus of the same institution. The parent reports the combined figures, and the child's own figures are blank or zero for that part. This app says so when a school's figures come from a related campus.
source: IPEDS overview 2019 (page 2: branch campuses); the IPEDS parent and child indicators

explanation: When a school does not report, or leaves some items blank, NCES estimates the missing figures so national totals are complete. Imputed figures are estimates, not the school's own report, and the IPEDS data files flag which figures were imputed.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Imputation; IPEDS overview 2019 (page 11)
app_convention: Imputed figures are shown as IPEDS publishes them, without a label.

explanation: Students attending college for the first time at the undergraduate level, at any school, and enrolled full time. They include students enrolled in the fall who first attended in the prior summer, and students who entered with college credit earned before finishing high school. Many IPEDS rates (graduation, retention, net price) are only about this group, not about all students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: First-time student (undergraduate); Full-time student

explanation: Fall enrollment counts students enrolled on the school's fall census date. 12-month enrollment counts every student enrolled at any time in a full year (July to June), each counted once. The 12-month count is larger, especially at community colleges with many short-term or part-time students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Fall Enrollment (EF); 12-month enrollment (E12)
app_convention: When you ask for enrollment, this app shows the fall total headcount, unless you ask for 12-month enrollment.

explanation: Instructional staff are people whose main job is teaching (or teaching with research or public service). Faculty status is a separate label the school gives some staff, often with rank and tenure. The two counts overlap but are not the same.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Instructional Staff; Faculty
app_convention: When you ask about faculty, this app asks which of these you mean.

concept: Pell grants as an income measure
explanation: IPEDS does not collect family income for all students. The share of undergraduates with a Pell Grant, which goes to students with financial need, is the usual stand-in for the share of lower-income students; it is a proxy, not a count of low-income students. IPEDS also reports net price by family income, for first-time, full-time students awarded federal (Title IV) aid.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Pell Grant program; Family income
app_convention: When you ask about low-income students, this app shows the share of undergraduates awarded Pell grants.

explanation: The graduation rate follows first-time, full-time students only, at 150% of normal time. Outcome Measures follow four groups (first-time and not first-time, full time and part time) and report awards at four, six and eight years, and where students without an award are enrolled. Outcome Measures describe more of a community college's students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Graduation rate; Outcome Measures (OM)

explanation: A school that awards associate's or higher degrees. Many IPEDS statistics, such as the NCES tables, cover degree-granting schools only.
source: IPEDS overview 2019; the IPEDS degree-granting status (DEGGRANT)

explanation: A classification of U.S. colleges by mission and the degrees they award, developed by the Carnegie Foundation and now kept by the American Council on Education. The 2024-25 IPEDS release carries the 2021 basic classification and the 2025 classifications (the institutional classification, the research designations, and student access and earnings). In this app, R1 and R2 mean the 2025 research designations; every Carnegie group names its classification, and in a trend a Carnegie group uses that classification as of 2024-25 for every year.
source: The Carnegie classifications IPEDS carries in 2024-25 (C21BASIC, CARNEGIEIC, CARNEGIERSCH); this app's own rules
app_convention: R1 and R2 use the 2025 research designation; a Carnegie group in a trend uses its classification as of 2024-25 for every year

words: GASB; FASB; finance forms; net position; net assets
explanation: Public schools report finance under government accounting standards (GASB). Private nonprofit schools report under the nonprofit standards of FASB, and for-profit schools also follow FASB standards, on a form of their own. The three forms name and group items differently, so finance figures are only roughly comparable across them.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26 (GASB and FASB entries)
app_convention: A finance figure for a group is shown separately for each form, since the three cannot be added together.

words: release year; academic year; fiscal year; data year
explanation: Each IPEDS release mixes periods. The 2024-25 release has fall 2024 enrollment, but completions, finance and net price for the year before (2023-24). This app shows each figure's own period beside it.
source: IPEDS variable titles and survey periods; this app's own rules

explanation: A blank in IPEDS can mean the school did not report the item, or that the item does not apply to it (a school with no graduate students reports no graduate enrollment). This app never counts either as zero, and says which one it is where IPEDS records it.
source: IPEDS special codes in the data files; this app's own rules

explanation: The admission rate is admitted applicants divided by all applicants, from schools that do not admit everyone. A low rate is often read as selectivity, but it also depends on how many students apply. IPEDS reports test scores and yield beside it.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26 (Applicant; Admissions)

explanation: Students who are admitted and intend to enroll in the spring, but do not show up in the fall. IPEDS does not measure it directly; the closest figures are the admission yield (admitted students who enrolled) and fall enrollment of first-time students.
source: General explanation (not in the glossary or the overview)

explanation: IPEDS has two kinds of private school: nonprofit and for-profit. In this app, "private" alone is read as private nonprofit; say "for-profit" to include those schools.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26 (Private not-for-profit institution; Private for-profit institution); this app's own rules

explanation: A U.S. Department of Education website that combines IPEDS data with federal student aid and tax records, for earnings, debt and repayment. Those earnings and debt figures are not in IPEDS.
source: General explanation
